key_big: Atomic number = protons; mass number = protons + neutrons.
body_html:
How to think about it

An atom has a small, dense, positive nucleus of protons and neutrons, with electrons in shells (K, L, M, N) around it. The atomic number Z is the number of protons; the mass number A is protons plus neutrons, so neutrons = A − Z.

Shells hold at most 2n² electrons, and the outermost shell holds at most 8. Valency is the number of electrons an atom loses or gains to get a full outer shell. Isotopes have the same Z but different A; isobars have the same A but different Z.

Example

Neutrons in ²³₁₁Na?

23 − 11

Answer: 12

Example

Configuration of sulphur (Z = 16)?

2 + 8 + 6

Answer: 2, 8, 6; valency 2

Common mistakes

  • Taking the mass number as the number of neutrons.
  • Putting more than 8 electrons in the outer shell of calcium (2, 8, 8, 2, not 2, 8, 10).
  • Mixing up isotopes and isobars.

faq.q: How is valency worked out from the configuration?
faq.a: If the outer shell has 1–4 electrons, valency equals that number; if it has 5–7, valency is 8 minus that number.

faq.q: Why do isotopes have the same chemical properties?
faq.a: They have the same number of electrons arranged in the same way.

sets.title: Particles and models of the atom

items.q: Why is an atom neutral overall?
c: it has no particles with charge
it has equal numbers of protons and electrons
items.e: The charges cancel.

items.q: Who discovered or proposed the electron, and the 'plum pudding' model of the atom?
items.e: J. J. Thomson: the electron, and the 'plum pudding' model of the atom.

items.q: Who discovered or proposed the nucleus, from the alpha-particle scattering experiment?
items.e: Ernest Rutherford: the nucleus, from the alpha-particle scattering experiment.

items.q: What is the mass number?
c: the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus
items.e: It is written as A.

items.q: Why are noble gases unreactive?
c: their outermost shell is full (an octet, or a duplet for helium)
items.e: Their valency is zero.

items.q: Why was gold foil used in Rutherford's experiment?
c: gold can be beaten into a very thin layer
items.e: The foil was about 1,000 atoms thick.

items.q: Which isotope is used as fuel in nuclear reactors?
items.e: Uranium-235 splits and releases energy.

items.q: What did Ernest Rutherford discover or propose?
c: electrons revolving in fixed orbits (shells) without radiating energy
the electron, and the 'plum pudding' model of the atom
the nucleus, from the alpha-particle scattering experiment
items.e: Ernest Rutherford: the nucleus, from the alpha-particle scattering experiment.

items.q: What did E. Goldstein discover or propose?
c: the nucleus, from the alpha-particle scattering experiment
canal rays, which led to the proton
electrons revolving in fixed orbits (shells) without radiating energy
items.e: E. Goldstein: canal rays, which led to the proton.

items.q: What is the charge and mass of an electron?
c: −1 charge and almost negligible mass (about 1/2,000 of a proton)
items.e: Protons are +1, neutrons have no charge; both are about 1 u.

items.q: What are isobars?
c: atoms with the same atomic number
atoms of different elements with the same mass number
items.e: Calcium-40 and argon-40 are isobars.

items.q: Who discovered or proposed canal rays, which led to the proton?
items.e: E. Goldstein: canal rays, which led to the proton.

items.q: What are nucleons?
items.e: They are the particles in the nucleus.

items.q: Which pair are isotopes?
items.e: Same atomic number, different mass numbers.

items.q: Which pair are isobars?
items.e: Same mass number, different atomic numbers.

items.q: What are valence electrons?
c: the electrons in the outermost shell
the electrons in the innermost shell
items.e: They decide how an atom reacts.

items.q: An atom has 7 electrons in its outermost shell. What is its valency?
items.e: It gains 1 electron, like chlorine.

items.q: What did James Chadwick discover or propose?
c: the electron, and the 'plum pudding' model of the atom
canal rays, which led to the proton
the nucleus, from the alpha-particle scattering experiment
items.e: James Chadwick: the neutron, in 1932.

items.q: Why do isotopes have the same chemical properties?
c: they have the same number of neutrons
they have the same electronic configuration
items.e: Their physical properties differ.

items.q: Who discovered or proposed the neutron, in 1932?
items.e: James Chadwick: the neutron, in 1932.

items.q: How many neutrons are there in an atom of silicon, <sup>28</sup><sub>14</sub>Si?
items.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 28 − 14 = 14.

items.q: An atom of boron has mass number 11 and 6 neutrons. How many protons does it have?
items.e: Protons = 11 − 6 = 5 (the atomic number).

items.q: How many neutrons are there in an atom of sodium, <sup>23</sup><sub>11</sub>Na?
items.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 23 − 11 = 12.

items.q: How many electrons are there in a neutral atom of neon (atomic number 10, mass number 20)?
items.e: A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons: 10.

items.q: How many neutrons are there in an atom of helium, <sup>4</sup><sub>2</sub>He?
items.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 4 − 2 = 2.

items.q: How many neutrons are there in an atom of lithium, <sup>7</sup><sub>3</sub>Li?
items.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 7 − 3 = 4.

items.q: An atom of phosphorus has mass number 31 and 16 neutrons. How many protons does it have?
items.e: Protons = 31 − 16 = 15 (the atomic number).

items.q: How many electrons are there in a neutral atom of lithium (atomic number 3, mass number 7)?
items.e: A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons: 3.

items.q: How many electrons are there in a neutral atom of hydrogen (atomic number 1, mass number 1)?
items.e: A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons: 1.

items.q: How many electrons are there in a neutral atom of sulphur (atomic number 16, mass number 32)?
items.e: A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons: 16.

items.q: An atom of argon has mass number 40 and 22 neutrons. How many protons does it have?
items.e: Protons = 40 − 22 = 18 (the atomic number).

items.q: An atom of silicon has mass number 28 and 14 neutrons. How many protons does it have?
items.e: Protons = 28 − 14 = 14 (the atomic number).

items.q: How many neutrons are there in an atom of nitrogen, <sup>14</sup><sub>7</sub>N?
items.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 14 − 7 = 7.

items.q: An atom of lithium has mass number 7 and 4 neutrons. How many protons does it have?
items.e: Protons = 7 − 4 = 3 (the atomic number).

items.q: How many electrons are there in a neutral atom of chlorine (atomic number 17, mass number 35)?
items.e: A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons: 17.

items.q: How many electrons are there in a neutral atom of phosphorus (atomic number 15, mass number 31)?
items.e: A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons: 15.

items.q: How many neutrons are there in an atom of chlorine, <sup>35</sup><sub>17</sub>Cl?
items.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 35 − 17 = 18.

items.q: How many electrons are there in a neutral atom of magnesium (atomic number 12, mass number 24)?
items.e: A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons: 12.

items.q: How many electrons are there in a neutral atom of boron (atomic number 5, mass number 11)?
items.e: A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons: 5.

items.q: How many neutrons are there in an atom of magnesium, <sup>24</sup><sub>12</sub>Mg?
items.e: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 24 − 12 = 12.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of argon (atomic number 18)?
items.e: Fill shells K, L, M, N with 2, 8, 8 …: 2, 8, 8.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of sulphur (atomic number 16)?
items.e: Fill shells K, L, M, N with 2, 8, 8 …: 2, 8, 6.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of nitrogen (atomic number 7)?
items.e: Fill shells K, L, M, N with 2, 8, 8 …: 2, 5.

items.q: Which element has the electronic configuration 2, 1?
items.e: 2 + 1 electrons in all, so the atomic number is 3: lithium.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of neon (atomic number 10)?
items.e: Fill shells K, L, M, N with 2, 8, 8 …: 2, 8.

items.q: Which element has the electronic configuration 2, 3?
items.e: 2 + 3 electrons in all, so the atomic number is 5: boron.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of carbon (atomic number 6)?
items.e: Fill shells K, L, M, N with 2, 8, 8 …: 2, 4.

items.q: Which element has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 1?
items.e: 2 + 8 + 1 electrons in all, so the atomic number is 11: sodium.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of silicon (atomic number 14)?
items.e: Fill shells K, L, M, N with 2, 8, 8 …: 2, 8, 4.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of aluminium (atomic number 13)?
items.e: Fill shells K, L, M, N with 2, 8, 8 …: 2, 8, 3.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of phosphorus (atomic number 15)?
items.e: Fill shells K, L, M, N with 2, 8, 8 …: 2, 8, 5.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of oxygen (atomic number 8)?
items.e: Fill shells K, L, M, N with 2, 8, 8 …: 2, 6.

items.q: Which element has the electronic configuration 2?
items.e: 2 electrons in all, so the atomic number is 2: helium.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of fluorine (atomic number 9)?
items.e: Fill shells K, L, M, N with 2, 8, 8 …: 2, 7.

items.q: Which element has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 8?
items.e: 2 + 8 + 8 electrons in all, so the atomic number is 18: argon.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of calcium (atomic number 20)?
items.e: Fill shells K, L, M, N with 2, 8, 8 …: 2, 8, 8, 2.

items.q: Which element has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 6?
items.e: 2 + 8 + 6 electrons in all, so the atomic number is 16: sulphur.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of magnesium (atomic number 12)?
items.e: Fill shells K, L, M, N with 2, 8, 8 …: 2, 8, 2.

items.q: Which element has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 2?
items.e: 2 + 8 + 2 electrons in all, so the atomic number is 12: magnesium.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of lithium (atomic number 3)?
items.e: Fill shells K, L, M, N with 2, 8, 8 …: 2, 1.

items.q: Which isotope is used to treat goitre?
items.e: Cobalt isotopes are used for cancer; uranium for nuclear reactors.

items.q: The electronic configuration of hydrogen is 1. What is its valency?
items.e: 1 outer electron, so the valency is 1.

items.q: The electronic configuration of boron is 2, 3. What is its valency?
items.e: 3 outer electrons, so the valency is 3.

items.q: The electronic configuration of carbon is 2, 4. What is its valency?
items.e: 4 outer electrons, so the valency is 4.

items.q: The electronic configuration of magnesium is 2, 8, 2. What is its valency?
items.e: 2 outer electrons, so the valency is 2.

items.q: What did Rutherford see when alpha particles hit a thin gold foil?
c: most passed straight through, a few were deflected and very few bounced back
items.e: So most of the atom is empty space with a small dense nucleus.

items.q: The electronic configuration of sodium is 2, 8, 1. What is its valency?
items.e: 1 outer electron, so the valency is 1.

items.q: What are isotopes?
c: atoms of different elements with the same mass number
atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers
items.e: Carbon-12 and carbon-14 are isotopes.

items.q: The electronic configuration of fluorine is 2, 7. What is its valency?
items.e: 7 outer electrons, so the valency is 1 (it needs 1 more for an octet).

items.q: The electronic configuration of phosphorus is 2, 8, 5. What is its valency?
items.e: 5 outer electrons, so the valency is 3 (it needs 3 more for an octet).

items.q: Where is almost all of the mass of an atom?
items.e: Protons and neutrons are much heavier than electrons.

items.q: The electronic configuration of beryllium is 2, 2. What is its valency?
items.e: 2 outer electrons, so the valency is 2.

items.q: The electronic configuration of oxygen is 2, 6. What is its valency?
items.e: 6 outer electrons, so the valency is 2 (it needs 2 more for an octet).

items.q: The electronic configuration of nitrogen is 2, 5. What is its valency?
items.e: 5 outer electrons, so the valency is 3 (it needs 3 more for an octet).

items.q: The electronic configuration of helium is 2. What is its valency?
items.e: 2 outer electrons, so the valency is 0.

items.q: The electronic configuration of potassium is 2, 8, 8, 1. What is its valency?
items.e: 1 outer electron, so the valency is 1.

items.q: What was a problem with Rutherford's model?
c: a revolving electron should lose energy and fall into the nucleus
items.e: Bohr solved this with fixed orbits.

items.q: The electronic configuration of lithium is 2, 1. What is its valency?
items.e: 1 outer electron, so the valency is 1.

items.q: The electronic configuration of argon is 2, 8, 8. What is its valency?
items.e: 8 outer electrons, so the valency is 0.

items.q: The electronic configuration of chlorine is 2, 8, 7. What is its valency?
items.e: 7 outer electrons, so the valency is 1 (it needs 1 more for an octet).
